t: In front of you is the bronze statue of Mary Seacole, standing in the grounds of St Thomas' Hospital and looking across the Thames towards the Houses of Parliament. It was made in 2016 by the sculptor Martin Jennings, and it's one of his largest works. Seacole was a Jamaican nurse and businesswoman, famous for her work in the Crimean War, where she ran what she called a British Hotel. She also wrote the first autobiography by a woman of African descent published in Britain. She was once voted first in a poll of one hundred Great Black Britons.
